以往体验市面上的各类 AI 电话助手，最让人顾虑的就是隐私安全：通话录音、转写文本、沟通对象全都会留在第三方云端。开发者刚刚开源的 ai-phone 则彻底打通了本地闭环——让你的 Mac 直接接管真实电话线路，所有推理均在本地完成，通话数据完全不出机器。

🛠️ 核心技术栈（基于 Apple Silicon & MLX）：

语音识别（STT）： Parakeet TDT 0.6B 本地运行，极速语音转文字

语言模型（LLM）： 默认本地运行 Qwen3.5 4B（32GB 内存支持 9B 4-bit），同时也支持接入自己的 Claude 或 ChatGPT 端点

语音合成（TTS）： Kokoro 82M / Phonon，生成自然流畅的声音

通信接入： 通过 SIP 协议直连 Telnyx 或 Twilio，直接购买或绑定真实电话号码（月租约 1 美元）

✨ 核心亮点：

低延迟与实时打断： 在 Apple Silicon 芯片上实测首字响应延迟约 1~1.5 秒；支持实时插话打断（Interruption），一旦你开口，AI 会立刻停下倾听。

支持外部 Agent 联动： 提供了 call、listen、say、hangup 等标准化 CLI 接口，可以直接让 Claude Code、Codex 等编码智能体通过命令编排通话，自动完成预约餐厅、电话咨询等任务。

本地守护进程： 提供向导式 CLI 配置，一行命令拉起本地守护进程，静默接听来电或随时发起外呼。

⚠️ 当前要求与限制：

仅支持搭载 Apple Silicon 的 macOS 系统

目前为单路通话，优先支持英文环境

项目刚刚上线，对本地 AI 语音助手与 SIP 通信落地感兴趣的朋友值得关注：https://t.co/n2G7fQGsnG

text:
This is completely f*cking wild.

A Stanford AI researchers gave Claude Code a second brain with JEV. The result? 80+ billion data points processed every 14 minutes.

here's how it works:

Jev stands at the door. every row has to get past it first.

the easy ones it waves through on the spot. only the ones it can't call get sent upstairs to Claude.

the old way:
everything -> Claude -> big bill

the new way:
everything -> Jev -> the tricky few -> Claude

Jev also tells you how sure it is on every call. that number decides who goes upstairs. just don't pick it out of thin air. test it first.

the 20-minute setup:

1. take 200 real rows from your data
2. run them through Jev AND Claude
3. sort Jev's answers by how sure it was
4. find the point where Jev stops disagreeing with Claude. that's your cutoff
5. above it, Jev's answer is final. below it, the row goes to Claude

then do the math. on a public benchmark Jev cost $0.015 per 1,000 rows and Claude cost $0.80.

if Jev settles 80% of your rows:

$0.015 + (20% × $0.80) = $0.175 per 1,000 rows instead of $0.80

that's ~78% off, with Claude still handling every hard case.

3 rules that keep it working:

-> ask all your questions in one Jev call. topic, urgency and sentiment together, not three separate requests
-> once a week, send 50 of Jev's "confident" answers to Claude anyway. if they start disagreeing, raise the cutoff
-> never let Jev make the final call on anything you can't undo. refunds, bans, deletions go to Claude or a human

where this pays off right away:

-> support tickets: route by topic and urgency
-> leads: hot, warm or skip
-> comments: fine, spam or needs a look
-> spreadsheets: fix category labels across thousands of rows

text:
Google just open-sourced Harness².

(turn any harness into a self-improving system)

a harness is everything wrapped around the model, like the system prompt, tools, memory, skills, and subagents. today a person designs it once, and the agent runs every new task with that same fixed setup.

Harness² lets the agent refine that setup for each new task on its own, with the model weights left untouched.

on every task, the agent proposes edits to its harness, runs a few candidate versions, and composes a better harness by comparing how those runs behaved.

because it learns from the differences between runs, it needs no correct answer or grader for the task.

that covers a single task. Harness² also carries what it learns from one task into the next.

after each task, it saves the harness it settled on along with the lessons that held up across the runs. the next time it refines a harness, it starts from those notes instead of from scratch.

this means every finished task makes the next round of edits more informed.

Google tested this with Gemini 3.5 Flash and GLM-5 on legal, office, and professional work benchmarks. one round of edits was enough to beat their original harnesses, and giving the agent more rounds pushed scores higher.

those extra rounds can go wide or deep. the agent either tries several candidate harnesses at once or keeps refining a single one step by step, using OpenCode or Codex to carry out the work.

you can find the Harness² repo here: https://t.co/i00WLeeFpw

I wrote about a similar idea for agents already running in production, where the harness should repair itself after a failure instead of waiting for someone to debug the trace by hand.

that piece walks through how @Cometml's Opik (open-source) closes this loop, going from a failing trace to a proposed fix to a regression test that stops the same failure from coming back. it's quoted below.

> state/build_state - goal, workers, done, missing, constraint. evidence, never a summary

• Jev decides (questions/)
> route - which model tier gets the task
> next_worker - which worker moves next
> relevance - keep or drop every tool output
> done - is the goal really met
> risky - will this send, pay or delete something?

• code acts (rules/)
> hard_rules - stop after ten actions, never publish anything unapproved
> thresholds.yaml - act only on confident answers. fraud needs 0.95

• Claude writes (workers/)
> research - sources and notes
> writer - drafts and briefings
> the one place in the folder where text gets generated

• the proof
> receipts/decisions.jsonl - options offered, chosen id, re-check, fallback
> evals/ - dozens of my own labelled traces, thresholds tuned on them

• the guards (hooks/)
> pre_tool_use - every command checked before it runs

Revisa ~/.claude/agents y .claude/agents para encontrar subagentes que ya cubran los roles explorer, worker y researcher.
